name: Bimetric Screened-Frame: Independent Stiff-Vector Lensing Chassis with e^-y PPN Decoupling
claimed_mechanism: This architecture introduces a second dynamical metric (h) interacting via Hassan-Rosen massive gravity to provide the off-ray lensing correction required to evade the DC-013 slip-lock. The preferred-frame vector u_mu mediates the MOND enhancement in dynamics, but its coupling to the lensing potential is strictly screened by e^-y. Crucially, the kinetic normalization of the massive graviton modes is set by the Hassan-Rosen parameters (m, c_i) and is entirely independent of the screened e^-y factor, thereby satisfying the P7 requirement that screening does not kill the kinetic term.
predicted_weak_field: In the weak-field limit, the massive graviton modes generate a finite contribution to the Newtonian potential and lensing that is not suppressed by the local acceleration y. The screened preferred-frame coupling ensures that PPN parameters alpha_1 and alpha_2 vanish exponentially in the Solar System (y >> 1), while the bimetric sector maintains a healthy, finite kinetic normalization for the propagating degrees of freedom, avoiding the strong-coupling wall that killed the khronometric candidate.
inequivalence_argument: This is inequivalent to DC-001 (frameless local) because it explicitly includes a preferred-frame carrier. It is inequivalent to DC-002 (AeST) because the lensing is carried by a massive bimetric sector with independent kinetic normalization, not a 6-DOF aether with constant K_B coupling. It is inequivalent to DC-010 (khronometric) because it does not use a khronon field; instead, it uses a bimetric sector to provide the finite kinetic norm, decoupling the screened PPN response from the propagating mode normalization.
